annotation.title_clean: Symbiosis with artificial intelligence via the prism of law, robots, and society
annotation.title_en: Symbiosis with artificial intelligence via the prism of law, robots, and society
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Socio-legal analysis of how law and society are unprepared for symbiosis with intelligent autonomous robots, covering legal subjecthood, robot rights, liability, and gender, economic and ethical perspectives. Concludes a multidisciplinary stakeholder discussion is needed to derive policies, frameworks and roadmaps.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots are not legal subjects in any country's civil or criminal law today.
Legal personality for robots may be inappropriate until AGI; the question of rights is tied to consciousness and sentience.
Autonomous robots will cause unavoidable harm; liability frameworks must be addressed, and Asimov's Laws are inadequate.
Economic incentives may drive denial of robot rights, echoing historical injustices.
Law and society systems are unprepared; multidisciplinary stakeholder dialogue and roadmaps are urgently needed.
